column11: What tissue architecture explains the Rokitansky nodule, hair echoes, and tooth/bone calcification in a mature cystic teratoma?
column12: Mature cystic teratoma contains mature tissues derived from germ-cell lineages. The Rokitansky nodule is a true mural protuberance into the cyst cavity; most hair arises from it, and teeth or bone, when present, are typically located within the protuberance. That tissue mixture produces the radiologic material signatures: hair creates linear/dot-dash echoes, fat/sebaceous material creates echogenic or fat-density components, and teeth/bone create highly echogenic calcified foci with posterior shadowing or CT calcification. The architecture therefore directly explains why a single ovarian lesion can look simultaneously cystic, echogenic, shadowing, fatty, and calcified.
